title: Company alignment zine: Q4 planning, OKR drafts, exec snapshot and all-hands runbook
body:
Purpose and tone: quick-read zine for execs + ICs. This is intentionally scrappy — use for rapid alignment, not the final deck. Goal: land a single coherent set of company OKR proposals + an actionable all-hands agenda + an exec update narrative we can ship to the board.

Snapshot (one-liner): Q4 focus = cost-per-inference optimization, Dedicated customer ramp, and Private SOC readiness. Keep the product surface stable for hosted customers while pushing optimizations that reduce unit cost.

Top-level proposed objectives (draft):
1) Objective: Reduce production unit economics gap (cost/token) to enable 25% higher throughput at same run cost.
  - KR1: Reduce mean inference cost per 1K tokens by 18% vs baseline (Sept 2026).
  - KR2: Improve average token throughput by 30% on Dedicated pools during peak windows.
  - KR3: Ship two optimizer features (KV-cache persistence + autoprefix caching) with integration docs.

2) Objective: Make Redwood Dedicated the predictable enterprise choice
  - KR1: Close 6 Dedicated contracts with >$200k ARR commitment.
  - KR2: Achieve 99.9% uptime for Dedicated clusters in-staging and one pilot customer in prod.
  - KR3: Create a Dedicated onboarding checklist that reduces time-to-first-traffic from 6 weeks to 3 weeks.

3) Objective: Launch Private deployment baseline for regulated customers
  - KR1: Complete V1 on-prem packaging and one customer pilot (healthcare).
  - KR2: Integrate KMS/HSM flows and generate audit report template.
  - KR3: Security signoff on data-at-rest and networking docs for SOC review.

Prioritization notes (quick):
- Must-haves: Dedicated SLOs, KV-cache persistence (big impact/noisy), and Private packaging for pilot customer.
- Consider: aggressive quantization for hosted catalog (good if we can validate quality regression <2% on core prompts).
- Defer: new model family onboarding unless tied to a specific customer commit.

All-hands run of show (90m):
- 00:00–00:05 Welcome + framing (CEO) — signal why Q4 narrow focus is critical.
- 00:05–00:20 Product pulse (Head of Product) — decisions on OKRs + demo of KV-cache.
- 00:20–00:35 Engineering highlight (serving-runtime) — failure-mode review + reliability wins.
- 00:35–00:50 Customer spotlight (CS) — Dedicated pilot case study (short).
- 00:50–01:05 Roadmap & how to help (Growth/SEs) — playbook for customer outreach.
- 01:05–01:25 Live Q&A (moderated) — collect top 12 questions via Slido.
- 01:25–01:30 Closing + next steps (CEO).

Rehearsal checklist (owners):
- Slides in company template (Elena) — due 2026-09-15
- Demo run and fallback video (Marcus) — due 2026-09-18
- Q&A prep + 12 canned answers (Priya) — due 2026-09-18
- Message to customers + blog draft (growth) — due 2026-09-20

Exec update narrative (2 paragraphs):
- Paragraph 1: Performance and economics: usage continues to grow (hosted monthly active endpoints +22% QoQ). Unit cost pressure remains primary risk — engineering’s optimization roadmap (KV-cache, batching improvements, kernel selection tuning) targets an 18–22% reduction in cost/token; early lab runs show ~12% on mixed workloads. We will prioritize ship-for-impact (features with measured cost delta) and pair each rollout with an internal eval.
- Paragraph 2: Go-to-market and adoption: Dedicated pipeline is healthy — we have 9 active opportunities, 3 at legal. Converting 2–3 of these in Q4 materially alters ARR trajectory. Private pilot timeline is tight but achievable with focused SRE + security bandwidth; recommend earmarking a single cross-functional team to unblock pilot in 6 weeks.

Decision log (rolling):
- 2026-08-25 — APPROVED: prioritize KV-cache persistence over model-family onboarding for Q4. Owner: Avery Chen. Rationale: highest cost impact and low external dependency.
- 2026-08-28 — ACTION: allocate 0.5 FTE security SME to Private pilot for 6 weeks. Owner: Priya Kapoor.
- 2026-09-01 — DISCUSSION: runbook for Dedicated failover needs a short-form cheat sheet for oncall. Owner: Marcus Liu (WIP).

Open questions / blockers:
- Can quantization be validated without customer-visible regressions on our top-20 prompts? (assigned to Applied ML, due 2026-09-10)
- Legal asks about international private deployment data residency — need definitive country list (Legal/Elena).
- Billing UX for Dedicated burst capacity is confusing for sales — quick fix required.

Action items (short):
- Marcus: repo of performance numbers + experiment plan (due 09/10).
- Priya: confirm security SME allocation + kickoff (due 09/07).
- Elena: final slides + speaker notes (due 09/15).
- Growth: draft customer comms announcing focus week + pilot invites (due 09/20).

Metrics appendix (compressed):
- Hosted usage: MAUs +22% QoQ, token volume +38% QoQ.
- Avg P95 latency (hosted): 140ms (target 120ms).
- Current mean cost per 1K tokens: $0.27 (target by end-Q4 $0.22).
- Dedicated pipeline: 9 active opps, 3 legal, 2 pilot commitments.

Notes to self / scratch:
- We should run a short internal A/B with 2 customers to validate quantization on chat workloads — avoid blanket rollout.
- Slack thread: #q4-focus-week (pin draft agenda and link to this doc).
- Cross-ref: confluence page for running experiments (CONFLUENCE-4321) and backlog ticket JIRA-OPS-1289.

Suggested next small-steps (tomorrow):
- Post this draft to #leadership-review with TL;DR and ask for one-sentence feedback by EOD.
- Schedule 30m cross-functional sync (Marcus/Priya/Elena/Avery) to validate timelines.

Tone reminders for all-hands: crisp, measurable, and non-alarmist. Focus on what teams can do (playbooks) vs. what we’ll fix centrally.

End of zine draft — treat as living.
